content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Order Backlog Growth", "construction": "From the annual 10-K, take the disclosed order backlog dollar amount (item often reported in the business/MD&A section). Compute year-over-year growth in backlog scaled by total assets: (Backlog_t - Backlog_{t-1}) / Average Total Assets. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Order backlog reflects contracted future demand not yet in revenue; the market underreacts to this leading indicator of future sales and earnings.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Deferred Revenue Change", "construction": "From the balance sheet, take the change in deferred (unearned) revenue over the trailing fiscal year, scaled by total assets: (DeferredRev_t - DeferredRev_{t-1}) / Total Assets. Sort stocks into deciles each June.", "rationale": "Rising deferred revenue signals customers prepaying for future delivery, a hard-cash leading indicator of future recognized revenue that investors underweight.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "R&D Momentum", "construction": "Compute the trailing three-year growth rate in R&D expense (Compustat XRD), scaled by lagged sales: geometric mean growth of XRD/Sales over three years. Rank cross-sectionally annually, restricting to firms with positive R&D.", "rationale": "Sustained increases in innovation investment presage future productivity and product-cycle gains that are mispriced due to conservative expensing of intangibles.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Supplier-Concentration Risk", "construction": "From 10-K disclosures of major customers (SFAS 131 segment/customer data), compute the fraction of revenue from customers each representing >10% of sales. Define concentration as the sum of these fractions. Sort into quintiles annually.", "rationale": "Firms dependent on few large customers bear elevated cash-flow risk and bargaining-power disadvantage, commanding a risk premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Working-Capital Efficiency Improvement", "construction": "Compute the cash conversion cycle (Days Inventory + Days Receivable - Days Payable) each year from Compustat. Take the year-over-year decline in the cash conversion cycle. Rank cross-sectionally; higher rank = larger improvement (larger decline).", "rationale": "Shortening the cash conversion cycle reflects operational improvements and freed-up cash that the market is slow to capitalize.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (larger reductions in the cycle)"}, {"name": "Intraday Range Volatility Compression", "construction": "For each stock, compute the average daily (High-Low)/Close range over the trailing 60 trading days, and the same over days 120-61. Define compression as the ratio of the recent range to the prior range; rank so that lower ratios (compressing ranges) rank high.", "rationale": "Compression of intraday trading ranges reflects declining disagreement and pending resolution of uncertainty, preceding positive drift as information stabilizes.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the ratio (greater compression)"}, {"name": "Pension Plan Funding Change", "construction": "From the pension footnote (SFAS 132), compute the change in funded status (plan assets minus projected benefit obligation) scaled by market equity, year-over-year. Rank into deciles annually.", "rationale": "Improving pension funding status frees future corporate cash flows from mandatory contributions and signals asset-management quality that investors overlook.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Selling-Expense Leverage", "construction": "Compute the ratio of change in sales to change in SG&A expense over the trailing year: (Sales_t - Sales_{t-1}) / (SGA_t - SGA_{t-1}), restricting to firms with positive SGA growth. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Firms generating disproportionately more revenue per incremental selling dollar exhibit operating leverage and scalable business models that predict rising margins.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Off-Balance-Sheet Lease Intensity Shift", "construction": "From lease commitment footnotes, capitalize operating lease obligations (discounted future minimum lease payments) and compute the year-over-year change in capitalized-lease-adjusted leverage relative to reported leverage. Rank annually.", "rationale": "Firms increasing reliance on off-balance-sheet operating leases carry hidden financial leverage and fixed-cost risk underappreciated by naive balance-sheet analysis.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (larger hidden-leverage increases)"}, {"name": "Analyst-Coverage Deceleration", "construction": "Using I/B/E/S, compute the change in the number of analysts covering a firm over the trailing 12 months, scaled by prior coverage. Rank so that stocks losing coverage rank high.", "rationale": "Declining analyst coverage reduces information production and visibility, raising the required return via an information-risk premium that later reverses upward.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the change (declining coverage)"}]}
